title: Odile and the Debt
premise: Ansel Vane, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of his family in row twelve of Flight 4471, is approached by a stranger named Odile who claims he saved her life years ago — a favor he never performed. The debt she insists on repaying drags him into a covert network that engineers 'attributable' disasters to move markets, and Ansel realizes row twelve was its first test. As Odile's identity fractures between ally, asset, and the network's most dangerous product, the two race to expose the trainers before Frankfurt's markets open and a manufactured catastrophe goes live. In the end Ansel burns the network's core from inside its own data center, Odile chooses to erase herself rather than be reclaimed, and Ansel finally learns row twelve was targeted because of him — a price of survival he must carry forward.
about_author: Wren Thackeray is the pen name of a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading the fine print of disasters. They write from a coastal town they refuse to name, and this is their second thriller.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Opening on the anniversary, Ansel revisits the wreckage report of Flight 4471 and the seat map with row twelve circled in his own handwriting. He can't stop investigating the crash that took his family, though every official channel has closed it. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into obsession.

chapters.title: The Favor
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A woman named Odile appears at his office claiming he pulled her from a burning car in Lyon — an accident Ansel knows he never attended. She insists the debt is real and must be repaid with interest, leaving a keycard and a time. Beat: unease curdling into compulsion.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile watches Ansel from a café, rehearsing a history she was trained to sell him, and we glimpse her handlers monitoring the meeting. She deviates from script by one sentence and immediately regrets it. Beat: a crack in her manufactured certainty.

chapters.title: Attributable
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Following the keycard to a dead storage unit, Ansel finds crash reports — dozens — each one a disaster that shifted markets within hours, each officially attributed to something banal. His family's file is among them, marked 'training data.' Beat: horror of recognition.

chapters.title: The Trainers
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ansel confronts Odile; she admits she was sent to recruit or neutralize him, but the debt story was her improvisation. She reveals the network — 'the Trainers' — engineers crises as live exercises for predictive trading algorithms. Beat: reluctant alliance forged in mutual leverage.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Countdown
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Odile shows him the network's next exercise: a staged infrastructure failure timed to Frankfurt's market open, nine days out, designed to be blamed on a dead patsy. Ansel recognizes the operational fingerprints from his own crash files. Beat: dread with a deadline.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reports partial compliance to her handler, Voss, buying Ansel time while concealing their alliance. A routine loyalty check forces her to burn a piece of her real past to protect the lie. Beat: the cost of double life.

chapters.title: The Patsy's Wife
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel tracks the designated patsy — a quiet rail engineer — and finds him already surveilled, his life pre-built for blame. Meeting the man's wife, who senses nothing, Ansel confronts what letting the exercise proceed would make him. Beat: moral weight of intervention.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Voss summons Odile for a debrief and probes her Lyon story; she realizes the 'favor' was itself a planted memory from her training. Her identity's foundation wobbles. Beat: vertigo of self-doubt.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel and Odile infiltrate a network front — a risk-analytics firm — and copy a fragment of the exercise schedule, learning the Frankfurt event has a backup trigger they can't yet locate. Beat: small victory shadowed by a larger unknown.

chapters.title: What the Algorithm Wants
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Decoding the fragment, they realize the exercises aren't for profit alone — the Trainers are teaching an algorithm to manufacture belief at scale, and row twelve was the lesson where they learned people believe grief. Beat: stakes widen from markets to minds.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. A rare antagonist chapter: Voss reviews Odile's file, notices the deviation, and decides not to correct it — instead scheduling her 'recertification' for the night before Frankfurt. Beat: cold, patient menace.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Tapes
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In a network safehouse, Ansel finds training recordings — including one of a young Odile being taught to grieve convincingly. He watches it alone and says nothing to her. Beat: love or trust beginning, contaminated by what he knows.

chapters.title: Recertification
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile is taken for recertification: sensory isolation, memory reinstallation, loyalty theater. She fights it from inside by anchoring to the one unscripted sentence she spoke in chapter three. Beat: identity as a battlefield.

chapters.title: Broken Extraction
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel runs a solo extraction, using the firm's own access protocols against it. He gets Odile out, but she surfaces uncertain which memories are hers — including whether her feelings for him were installed. Beat: rescue that doesn't feel like one.

chapters.title: The Backup Trigger
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Rebuilt trust through honesty — Ansel confesses to the tapes; Odile confirms what's real and what isn't. Together they identify the backup trigger: a second, human cost, someone who must die for the Frankfurt event to complete. Beat: intimacy rebuilt on truth.

chapters.title: The Human Cost
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The designated death is the patsy's wife — the network tying off its loose thread. Ansel and Odile split: he goes to protect her, Odile to the data center where the algorithm's final weights are staged. Beat: the plan fraying under time pressure.

chapters.title: Eight Hours to Open
chapters.summary: Dual POV, interleaved. Night before market open. Ansel shelters the wife through a first assassination attempt; Odile infiltrates the Frankfurt data center and discovers the exercise can be rerouted — but only from inside the burn. Beat: ticking-clock dread.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer
chapters.summary: Voss's POV shifting to Odile. Voss corners Odile in the data center and offers her everything: her real history, her real name, a life outside the network — if she walks away and lets Frankfurt happen. Beat: temptation rendered as mercy.

chapters.title: The Burn
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, then Odile's. Odile refuses Voss and initiates the burn from inside as Ansel, having saved the wife, breaches to cover her. The algorithm's weights are destroyed mid-training; Voss is caught in the collapse of his own contingency. Beat: climax — fire, sacrifice, choice.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Attributed
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Frankfurt opens on an ordinary day; the world never knows what almost moved it. Official inquiries close with tidy, banal explanations — the network's own habit turned to cover. Odile is gone, leaving only the Lyon keycard. Beat: hollow, necessary victory.

chapters.title: The Debt Repaid
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, closing. Ansel reopens his family's case with the evidence he salvaged, and finally visits row twelve's memorial. A postcard arrives, unsigned, from a city he can't place: 'Favor returned.' Beat: grief integrated, identity survived, the price acknowledged.
